title: Major depressive disorder shares systemic immune signatures and potential therapeutic targets with inflammatory skin diseases
projectDescription: This dataset contains normalized protein expression (NPX) values from Olink proteomic profiling of serum from patients with major depressive disorder, atopic dermatitis, psoriasis, and healthy controls, using the proximity extension assay technology across four panels: Target 96 Inflammation, Cardiovascular II, Cardiovascular III, and Neurology.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Blood was drawn into Vacutainer Gold Top 5 mL Silica Gel tubes (BD, #365968). Blood was allowed to clot for >30 min, centrifuged at 1300 g for 15 min at 4°C, then aliquoted and stored at -80°C. Serum aliquots from subjects were analyzed using the high-throughput proteomic Olink Proseek multiplex assay (Olink Proteomics, Uppsala, Sweden), as previously described (15, 16, 35). Serum levels of 353 proteins derived from four panels (General Inflammation, Neurological Inflammation, Cardiovascular Disease II, Cardiovascular Disease III) were quantified.
dataProcessingProtocol: Analyses were performed with R language (www.R-project.org) using publicly available Bioconductor packages (www.bioconductor.org). Fold changes (FCs) were estimated, and hypothesis testing was conducted using contrasts under the general framework for linear models using the limma package, adjusting for age, sex, and body mass index (BMI) as covariates. P-values were adjusted for multiple comparisons using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure to control for false discovery rate (FDR). Proteins with |FC|>1.2 and P<0.05 or FDR<0.05 were considered differentially expressed.
